items.evidence: The MCC assigned an overall 2019 CIP Corporate Performance Rating of 0.95 reflecting mixed results across all categories.
Earnings —2019 reported earnings of $2.9 billion was below Plan, reflecting Upstream impairment and write-offs totaling $10.4 billion
Cash flow —Chevron delivered operating cash flow of $27.3 billion in 2019, supported by strong production growth.
Divestiture proceeds —$2.8 billion in asset sales proceeds were realized for the year.
capital management—30 percent
Return on capital employed —Reported ROCE for 2019 of 2.0 percent was below Plan, mainly driven by lower earnings.
Capital and exploratory expenditures —2019 organic C&E totaled $20.2 billion, in-line with budget.
Major milestones per Plan:
operating performance—15 percent
Net production of 3.087 million barrels of oil-equivalent per day in 2019, excluding divestments.
Operating expense totaled $25.9 billion, above Plan, with a slight increase in unit costs.
Refining utilization rates were below Plan by 3.7 percentage points.
health, environmental and safety—15 percent
Personal Safety—Maintained industry-leading Days Away From Work rate and achieved record low Serious Injury count for the Company.
Loss of containment performance and spill volume was better than Plan, with some gaps in severity.
Greenhouse gas management—on-track to achieve flaring and methane intensity reductions.
The MCC also takes into account individual performance. This is largely a personal leadership dimension
Payout is dependent on Chevron's TSR over a three-year period, compared with our LTIP Performance Share Peer Group TSR.
RSUs | 25% | Actual number of RSUs granted is determined by dividing the proportionate value of the NEO's LTIP award
Stock options | 25% | Strike price is equal to Chevron's closing common stock price on the grant date.
